title: introduce-invocation-flamegraph-and-cost-sparkline-aggregator
author: Marcus Liu
description:
Summary: Add a low-cardinality invocation flamegraph aggregator and a lightweight cost-sparkline panel to surface per-invocation phase latency and token-cost trends in a single view. Motivation: Operators need a quick way to see which phases (parse/prefetch/kv/cache/compute/emit) dominate cost and latency across cohorts without exploding cardinality in metrics backends. This PR introduces a hybrid approach: server-side hierarchical rollups (flame nodes with aggregated token-cost) plus a client Grafana panel that draws an interactive flamegraph and overlays cost sparklines for the selected invocation group.

Design: 1) ingestion: new aggregator service (observability/ingest/flame-aggregator) consumes sampled span-phase timing tuples (phase, duration_ms, token_count) and produces per-invocation_group hierarchical rollups every 30s. Each rollup includes node id, parent id, accumulative token-cost (tokens * phase_weight), mean and p95 duration, and a 32-bit cost_signature fingerprint to avoid high-cardinality label explosion. Rollups are compact JSON lines and stored in the telemetry object store with TTL-based retention. 2) storage: rollups indexed by time window + invocation_group + cost_signature. This keeps cardinality bounded while enabling fast drilldowns. 3) frontend: Grafana plugin (panels/flame-spark) that fetches rollup windows and renders a flamegraph; hover shows per-node token-cost and duration distributions; a mini-sparkline strip shows cost trend for the selected node across the last N windows. 4) sampling: default sample rate 1% for normal traffic, 10% for canary/synthetic routes; rate configurable by route. 5) safety: memory and CPU caps on aggregator, backpressure to the trace pipeline, and a fallback that writes raw phase metrics if aggregation is unavailable.

Migration/Rollout: Start with a staged rollout: enable aggregation for a small set of internal routes behind a feature flag for 72h, verify storage and query latencies, then flip to 25% of traffic and monitor cost/disk; final rollout to 100% after two successful windows. Linear tickets ENG-4123 and ENG-5321 track the rollout and UX polish.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement aggregator service and protobuf schema for phase tuples.
- [x] Add indexer + storage writer with TTL.
- [x] Implement Grafana panel and wire to frontend build pipeline.
- [x] Add unit + integration tests for aggregator and panel.
- [x] Add route-level sampling config and feature flag.
- [x] Add docs: observability/README and dashboard runbook.
- [x] Perf smoke tests and mem/cpu limits.

Notes: The cost_signature is intentionally short (32-bit) to trade perfect uniqueness for cardinality control; the UI surfaces collisions and allows narrow-time window replays to disambiguate. This PR intentionally avoids adding high-cardinality labels to metrics streams; instead we store rollups in the object store indexed by compact keys. The aggregator is implemented in Go and uses a sharded in-memory accumulation map with periodic flush to avoid high-tail GC pauses.

Risk: Moderate — new ingestion path and storage. Mitigations are staged rollout, strict caps, and a deprecation path to fall back to raw phase metrics.

How to validate: follow runbook in observability/docs/invocation-flamegraph.md (includes queries, thresholds, and manual replay instructions).

review_comments: Priya Nambiar (reviewer): Could you explain the cardinality math for invocation_group + cost_signature? I'm worried about bursty routes creating too many signatures.

Marcus Liu (author): We limit the signature entropy by hashing only normalized prompt shape + model_id + truncated route key; combined with 30s window this gives a practical bound. Added details to docs.
Ethan Park (reviewer): e2e panel test timed out in CI; looks like the frontend waits for rollups. Can we add a timeout and a graceful fallback?
Marcus Liu (author): Added a 5s timeout and a spinner fallback that shows raw phase metrics when rollups are not available; updated ci/dashboard-e2e.yml to allow longer startup. CI rerun passed.
Lucia Moreno (reviewer): Memory cap on aggregator looks low for 10% sampling on heavy routes; can we set a stricter eviction policy?
Marcus Liu (author): Increased shard eviction threshold and added LRU node eviction with logging; also added metrics to alert if eviction rate > 0.5% per window.
release_notes: Add invocation flamegraph and cost-sparkline aggregator for phase-level cost and latency visibility. Includes a Grafana panel (flame-spark) and server-side rollups to keep metric cardinality low. Staged rollout behind feature flag.
notes: Staged rollout recommended; initial internal-only enablement validated CPU and disk usage. See observability/docs/invocation-flamegraph.md for runbook and queries.
observability_impact: New flamegraph rollups provide per-phase token-cost and duration p95 without adding high-cardinality metric labels. Enables faster SRE triage for long-tail latency and cost regressions.
